[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
John Glasgow was born in 1722 and died in 1769. He was originally buried in the Nottingham Presbyterian Old Church Yard across from what is now Rising Sun Middle School in Maryland.<ref name="glasgowbible">Glasgow Family Bible, York Historic Trust Museum and Genealogy Library, York, Pennsylvania.</ref> According to the Glasgow Family Bible, he was buried alongside his wife Mary (Cranmer) Glasgow and their son John Glasgow II.

In 1959, the West Nottingham Church Historian recorded that the congregation decided to relocate the old burial ground. Only 45 graves were found and 25 were identified. In 1960, the remains were reinterred at West Nottingham Church Cemetery. Today, John Glasgow Sr. and John Glasgow II are buried next to each other there.<ref name="glasgowbible" />

The Glasgow Family Bible, originally belonging to John Glasgow II, was later passed to his son Congressman [[Glasgow-2873|Hugh Glasgow (1769-1818)]], who is buried at Slate Ridge Cemetery, York County. The Bible remains documented at the York Historic Trust Museum and Genealogy Library.<ref name="glasgowbible" />

=== Possible Parentage and Family Connections ===


An unproved wider family connection has been suggested between John Glasgow and [[Glasgo-52|John Glasgo (abt.1772-1851)]], who married [[Boydston-414|Amelia Boydston (1778-1857)]]. Jeremiah Glasgow, likely [[Glasgo-23|Jeremiah Glasgow (1713-1777)]], witnessed the will of David Boydston, Amelia’s father.<ref name="boydstonwill">Will of David Boydston, cited in Boydston Family Records. [https://www.genealogy.com/ftm/b/a/t/Margaret-R-Bates/GENE15-0008.html]</ref>

The family account identifies [[Glasgow-2871|John Glasgow (1738-1792)]] as a son and also attributes [[Glasgow-2872|Samuel Glasgow (1761-1824)]] to this family and the Nottingham Old Presbyterian burial ground at Rising Sun, Maryland. Samuel’s parentage and burial attribution require independent checking; his preferred Irish father is discussed below, while the Bible narrative explicitly concerns Mary and son John.

== Research Notes ==
=== Samuel’s disputed parentage ===

The Bible account describes John’s burial with his wife Mary and son John, followed by the Bible’s transmission to Congressman Hugh. No inspected literal entry names [[Glasgow-2872|Samuel Glasgow]] as John’s son. Samuel is identified at 98% with the West Fallowfield testator whose will names Tabitha, infant Margaret Ellen and three brothers William, James and Robert in Ireland. The memorial’s Judith and later Tabitha family, together with the Chester deed index, supply a specific identity bridge. John is now an '''unselected uncertain father alternative, 25%''', formerly 72%; [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] is the preferred replacement at '''67% probable'''. The matching Irish brother configuration is positive evidence, while the will and stone name no father.<ref name="SamuelChesterComparison">Chester County estate 7520, [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=773006&page=588&repo=r-24f48cc6 will 17 May 1824, proved 31 May, portal pp.588–589]; [https://www.chesco.org/DocumentCenter/View/84215/E-G#page=940 official deed index E–G, PDF p.940], West Fallowfield entries A3:435, A3:433, Y2:391 and K3:394 (actual deeds unread); [https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/75056130/samuel_glasgow memorial 75056130], current family display and Theresa Ely stone photograph, reviewed 24 October 2026. Contributor vital dates are not independent proof; stone age unread.</ref>

Faris’s anonymous family recollection names James and Margaret Rutherford’s four sons, including Samuel who went to America; its retrospective nature leaves the precise Chester identification and chronology uncertain. Samuel’s reported 1761 Pennsylvania birth and John/Mary attribution remain competing claims. If that birth and the alleged 1759 death of James-1025 were proved, they could defeat the Irish route. Margaret Rutherford’s estimated 1700 birth and Samuel-1492’s estimated 1726 birth remain unresolved; no merge, maternal reassessment or vital correction follows. The four Irish father grades 78/76/77/84% and the older William grade32% are unchanged. John’s Bible and Scottish1722 evidence retain their separate scope.<ref name="SamuelIrishFamily">David Faris, ''The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio'' (1990), printed pp.8–12, especially [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-J p.9]; [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ Albert Rutherford’s anonymous family-letter transcription]. Faris cites T1959/file5, Rutherford T1959/3; original letter uninspected and the reproductions are not independent witnesses.</ref>

=== Libberton record-parent review — 17 October 2026 ===

'''Parent-role review, 17 October 2026:''' Robert Glasgow and Katherin Wilson are '''documented parents of the Scottish child baptised at Libberton in 1722'''. The child’s identification with the later American John remains unproved; this is not documented American ancestry.

The accepted Findmypast transcript for John Glasgow’s Libberton baptism on 23 September 1722 explicitly names father Robert Glasgow and mother Katherin Wilson, with residence Sandyburgh: OPR 650/1, page 17, item 3, SCOT/OPR/BAP/4033399. [[Glasgow-3407|Robert Glasgow]] is the maintained Wilson-household father account and [[Wilson-127539|Katherine Wilson]] its mother account. These are two explicit parental names in one baptism transcript, not a mother inferred from a husband’s surname. The existing Carnwath 1713 Robert–Katherine Wilson marriage citation is compatible household context; it is not needed to invent the 1722 parents or to treat every local Robert as the same man.

The documented assessment applies to the Scottish child and parents in the 1722 baptism. The later American identity attributed to John—Nottingham, Chester County, and a May 1769 death—remains unproved. The profile’s Bible and burial citations have not supplied an inspected migration, household or parent bridge from Libberton. The American newspaper comparisons remain qualified. This does not establish that the American John had these parents. The source supplies a baptism date, not an independently proved birth date. Katherin in Findmypast and Katharin in the retained MyHeritage index are provider spelling variants of the record’s Wilson mother, not two independent maternal confirmations. The source is the transcript captured on 3 September 2026; the original register image has not been inspected.

The Scottish baptism does not prove the descendant chain in America. Robert’s own selected [[Glasgow-3332|James Glasgow]] father, competing Johne route and birth estimate remain uncertain. The separate Gibson/Watson Robert family must not be combined with the Wilson household. John’s Scottish parent assessments retain their existing scope; no migration or American ancestry is established.

<ref name="LibbertonParents2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4033399&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births & Baptisms, John Glasgow, 23 September 1722, Libberton, Sandyburgh; Robert Glasgow and Katherin Wilson; OPR 650/1 p.17 item3, SCOT/OPR/BAP/4033399; transcript captured 3 September 2026, re-reviewed here]; [https://www.myheritage.com/research/record-30226-745324/john-glasgow-in-scotland-births-baptisms MyHeritage Scotland Births and Baptisms index, John Glasgow, Libberton 1722, Robert and Katharin Wilson; alternative presentation of the same register event].</ref>

[https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/early-scottish-records/#chapter-libberton-record-parents-confidence Full comparison and remaining questions].

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Nottingham merchant and vendue attendee. John Glasgow signed a notice for a 2 September 1760 public vendue for creditors of deceased William Graham, including a 200-acre patent tract on the Susquehanna near Shepard's Ferry in Cecil County, Maryland; he also intended to open a store in Nottingham by the end of September.<ref>Pennsylvania Gazette, 14 August 1760, p.3, image 39404812; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/39404812/ record].</ref> The notice names no kin or origin. It does not establish Irish birth or migration. The identification remains uncertain.

=== Possible John Glasgow, Kensing-/ton postal entry, 1769 ===
John Glasgow, Kensing- / ton, is an addressee in letters remaining at Philadelphia post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39396485/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1769-10-26, p.1].</ref>

The place is printed over two lines as Kensing-/ton. The list does not establish a modern jurisdiction or family; it could include mail for a deceased addressee.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2870]]. Regional namesake; no Kensing-/ton postal connection. Recorded earlier death does not rule out posthumous mail.

=== Possible John Glasgow, Nottingham/Chester postal and near-Oxford book records, 1758–1771 ===
John Glasgow, Nottingham, is an addressee in letters remaining at Philadelphia post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39389283/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1758-01-12, p.1].</ref>

John Glasgow, in Nottingham Township, Chester County, is an addressee in letters remaining at Chester post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1033731085/ The Pennsylvania Journal, or, Weekly Advertiser, 1765-10-17, p.1].</ref>

John Glasgow, Nottingham, is an addressee in letters remaining at Chester post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39406491/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1765-11-28, p.4].</ref>

John Glasgow near Oxford is listed among people taking in subscriptions for De Jure Regni; advertisement dated 22 May 1766.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39391550/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1766-05-29, p.4].</ref>

John Glasgow, in West Nottingham, Chester County, and William Glasgow are separate addressees in the Charles-Town, Maryland, post-office list headed 1 October 1771.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41041559/ Maryland Gazette, 1771-10-24, p.3].</ref>

These entries form a qualified regional comparison, not a proved single life. A John who died in May 1769 could be the earlier collector/addressee; the 1771 letters could concern his surviving son, another man or posthumous mail. The separately listed William is not proved to be a relative.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2870]]. Exact Nottingham/Chester County death-place comparison and compatible age fit the earlier Nottingham/near-Oxford records, but underlying personal identity sources have not been freshly checked. The later 1771 postal entry could be posthumous mail or another man.

=== Findmypast record review, 24 October 2026 ===

Glasgow-2870 as Scottish record-defined baptised child only; his later American/Nottingham identity remains unproved.. The companion index repeats the known Libberton baptism on 23 September 1722, naming Robert Glasgow and Katharin Wilson, with male sex and broad Libberton residence. It matches the Scottish record-defined child account under Glasgow-2870 and the held SCOT/OPR/BAP/4033399 event; its broad locality does not supersede the held Sandyburgh detail. Glasgow-3407 and Wilson-127539 are the retained Scottish parent-profile roles. Neither index establishes an exact birth or bridges the Scottish child to the later Nottingham/Pennsylvania adult. The inherited exact birth field is retained pending its separate basis review.<ref name="FMP19Glasgow28700">Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564-1929, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_684956583&tab=this R_684956583]; derivative transcript inspected 24 October 2026; original uninspected.</ref>

Original registers and inscriptions remain uninspected. Companion entries repeat an event rather than independent corroboration. No new person or relationship regrade is proposed. Current vital fields remain unchanged; baptism-only or age-derived fields do not independently prove exact births.
